data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":null,"claim":"The simulation must be filed to produce the exact counts and calibration trace; however, the 2-sigma criterion corresponds to a 95% confidence interval, meaning a truly fair generator has a ~5% chance of failing it, so the outcome must be interpreted as a continuous statistical measurement rather than a strict deterministic verdict (simulation proposal filed).","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the simulation and calibration trace are not successfully filed, the epistemic argument lacks the necessary empirical grounding.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the problem's definition of 'fair' is interpreted strictly as a binary pass/fail rule, the statistical nuance of this candidate is overridden.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"The problem specifies a two-standard-deviation bound, which in normal approximation corresponds to a 95% interval.
